title: Member system registration (foundational)
description: Each independently managed archive registers with the federation: its identifier, access endpoint, data classes, and its own local access policy. Registration is explicit and versioned; unregistered systems are invisible to the federation. The registry is the federation's source of truth about who participates. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Archive Federation Controller practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Cross-system permission mapping (foundational)
description: Each member's local roles are mapped to federation-wide capabilities through an explicit mapping table. A 'researcher' in archive A and a 'reader' in archive B might both map to the federation's 'read-public' capability. Mapping tables are maintained per member and reviewed when either side's policy changes. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Archive Federation Controller practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Access brokering for cross-system requests (foundational)
description: When a user requests data from another member system, the controller brokers the request: it checks the federation mapping, forwards the request with the mapped capability, and enforces the remote system's decision. The broker never overrides a member's local policy; it coordinates, not commands. Denials are returned with the reason, not silently dropped. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Archive Federation Controller practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Consistency coordination across members (foundational)
description: For data replicated across members, the controller coordinates consistency: writes go through a primary, and replicas acknowledge within a bounded window. Readers are told the consistency level they are getting, such as read-your-write or eventual. Coordination keeps the federation's view coherent without requiring every member to run the same software. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Archive Federation Controller practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Federation audit of cross-system access (foundational)
description: Every brokered access is logged with the user, the mapped capability, the member system, and the decision. The audit log lets each member see exactly what the federation did in its name. Logs are shared back to members on request, closing the accountability loop. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.

print('federation audit entries:', len(audit))
